chapter: Learning the trade in Los Angeles
title: Earl Dancer forms a studio band; Parker Berry
summary: Former Ethel Waters manager Earl Dancer got movie-studio work and formed his own band, with trombonist Parker Berry doing the arranging.

story.theme_name: Writing and arranging: how musicians compose
story.community_name: Writing, arranging and composing: how the music gets made

blocks.x: Oh, I stayed with Ecc for a long time until a fellow came to California named Earl Dancer. He'd just come from New York. He used to be Ethel Waters' manager. And he had some big ideas. He was a good talker and a good promoter. And he went right into the studios and then he, he used to get all the studio work for bands. He knew some of the big shots that had been in New York and now they were stars in the studios.
So when they saw Earl, he could get a lot of jobs that Echols couldn't get. So he finally got the idea of forming his own band and keeping the band working in the studios making pretty good money.
When you talk of studios, you mean movie studios?

Movie studios, yes. So he knew Busby Berkeley who had all of these big spectacular shows and millions of chorus girls dancing. So the band, Echols band kind of split. One went one way and the other went, the other stayed with Echols.
But I went with Earl. I went with Earl Dancer.
Now he wasn't a musician really?
He was no kind of musician.
Yes. He didn't know anything except he knew night life. He knew show business. But he definitely wasn't a musician.
With a white suit and baton.
Well who was the straw boss ?

A fellow named Parker Berry. A trombone player. I don't know where Parker is now. I think he's somewhere in Texas. He did all the arranging and he really ran the band. And Earl was the leader, but really Earl didn't know what to tell us to do. So Parker did it. Parker, he was the one that taught me how to arrange music. And a lot of other things He used to teach me.
